newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Raul Salinas to testify - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Raul Salinas to testify - paper.

text.p: The jailed brother of Mexico's ex-President Carlos Salinas has offered to make a videotaped cassette to be used as testimony to defend a former Mexican official facing trial in a U.S. court, La Jornada newspaper said on Saturday.
The newspaper said Raul Salinas would deny accusations that former Mexican Deputy Attorney General Mario Ruiz Massieu took money to protect drug traffickers.

Citing court documents from pre-trial hearings in Houston, La Jornada said defence attorneys for Ruiz Massieu asked Salinas, imprisoned for the past two years outside Mexico City, to testify on their client's behalf.
The newspaper said defence lawyer Tony Canales argued that Salinas was the only witness who could defend Ruiz Massieu against government charges he accepted drug money.

U.S. prosecutors are seeking to confiscate $9 million from a Houston bank account held by Ruiz Massieu, saying he was paid the money by drug traffickers seeking protection. The case is set of March 10.
Ruiz Massieu has said in pre-trial depositions that the money sought by the U.S. government was family money deposited in Texas to protect it from economic and political uncertainty in Mexico.
Salinas is facing charges of masterminding in September 1994 the assassination of Ruiz Massieu's brother, Jose Francisco, a former top ruling party official.
